summary: Bradford's infrastructure positions center on accelerating construction, reducing congestion, and delivering basic services. Bradford repeatedly advocated for 24/7 construction on the Gardiner Expressway, off-site prefabrication, and the creation of a Congestion Relief Commissioner / "Traffic Czar" to coordinate competing projects. Bradford opposed tearing down the Gardiner and supported the Province uploading the Gardiner and DVP. On winter operations, Bradford characterized snow clearing as a core service, criticized multi-week response times, and proposed prioritizing school zones, main roads, sidewalks, and transit access. Bradford championed "complete streets," road-design-based safety, traffic calming, cycling infrastructure including the Danforth bike lanes, EV charging, and community facilities (Dawes Road Library, Weston Lions Arena, Ontario Science Centre). Bradford opposed the $150M West Toronto Railpath extension and a Foxbar Road median, while supporting open tendering and intergovernmental partnership to fund infrastructure.

key_positions.stance: Supports 24/7 construction and off-site prefabrication to accelerate the Gardiner Expressway rebuild
Supports creating a Congestion Relief Commissioner / 'Traffic Czar' to coordinate construction across governments
Opposes tearing down the Gardiner Expressway
Supports treating snow removal as a core city service with prioritization of main roads, sidewalks, school zones, and transit access
Opposes multi-week snow response timelines and inadequate winter maintenance
Supports 'complete streets' and road-design-based safety over punitive enforcement
Supports investment in cycling infrastructure including Destination Danforth bike lanes and Woodbine bike lanes
Opposes the $150M West Toronto Railpath extension as unreasonable spending
Supports protecting and investing in community facilities (Weston Lions Arena, Dawes Road Library, Ontario Science Centre, Secord School)
Supports keeping parallel routes open and not closing them simultaneously during construction
Supports intergovernmental (federal/provincial/city) partnership to fund infrastructure
Supports EV charging infrastructure including front yard parking pads and on-street chargers
Supports open tendering for construction contracts
Supports flood mitigation and basement flooding protection programs
